audit: SAT Math concept-repeat check at 106 accepted

repeats.why: Same item shell: store sells two package sizes, equation ax+by=total represents shipment, given count of larger size find count of smaller; near-identical wording.
Line y = x + k tangent to circle x^2+y^2=r^2 centered at origin, k>0, find k; near-identical wording (50 vs 8).
Exponential function with f(0)=5 that triples per unit step, find f(4): same numbers (5, x3, answer 405); only table vs verbal presentation differs.
Solve a 2x2 linear system and report a combination of x and y (x+y vs x-y).
Demo fixture: 2x+y=11, x-y=1, find x+y - same system-then-x+y ask as 3x+2y=19, x-y=3.
Both: simplify a squared binomial minus another quadratic product, (2x-3)^2-(x+1)^2 vs (3x-2)^2-(x+1)(9x-5); same expand-and-combine routine.
Arc length from radius and a radian central angle, s = r*theta (15, 4pi/5 vs 4, 1.5).
Both find the middle coefficient b making a trinomial a perfect square (one real solution <=> perfect square); both answers are 12.
Positive b making ?x^2+bx+9 a perfect-square trinomial (4x^2 vs x^2, both constant 9).
Percent of a percent of a total (35% then 25% of 240 vs 30% of 40% of 500); SAT adds survey context only.
Two supplementary angles given as linear expressions in x (same-side interior vs consecutive parallelogram angles); sum to 180 and report one angle.
Both: single linear equation with one distributed binomial on the left, variable on both sides (5(t-3)+2=3t+9 vs 5(x-2)=3x+4).
Convert a speed between unit systems (m per min to km per h vs in per s to ft per min).
"Which value of x satisfies" a linear inequality whose solving requires flipping the inequality for a negative coefficient.
Line y=2x+k meets/tangent to a parabola (y=x^2 vs y=x^2+3) at exactly one point; set discriminant to 0 and find k.
Demo fixture: y=x^2+k and y=4x have exactly one solution, find k - same tangency/discriminant setup and ask.
Monic quadratic x^2+bx+c with roots a fixed distance apart (6 vs 4), find c.
Right triangle whose legs are in a known ratio (3:4 vs 1:1) with given area, find hypotenuse.
Choose the exponential model for a quantity changing by a fixed percent per period (6% growth monthly vs 4% decay hourly).
Two pricing plans, find the least whole number of units at which one plan becomes cheaper (strict-inequality break-even).
Known mean of n values, one value added to reach a new target mean, find that value (3 tests 84->87 vs 9 values 12->13).
Demo fixture: given five quiz scores, find sixth score so the mean is 86 - same target-mean ask.
Demo fixture: 3x+5=20, find 6x+10 vs x/4=9, find x/12 - evaluate a scaled related expression without (or after) solving.
2x2 linear system with unknown coefficient(s) having infinitely many solutions; make the equations proportional.
Use (x+y)^2 = x^2+y^2+2xy linking sum, product, and sum of squares (SAT finds (x+y)^2, ACT finds x^2+y^2).
Line with given slope through two points, one containing unknown k; set slope formula equal and solve for k.
a(x-2)=bx+c, "What value of x satisfies": 5(x-2)=3x+4 vs 3(x-2)=2x+5.
Quadratic with two equal outputs (symmetry gives vertex x) plus a known min/max value, evaluate f at another point.
Apply a part-to-whole rate (3 of 8 / 18 of 60) to a larger population to find the expected count.
Demo fixture: arc length from radius 6 and central angle 120 deg (degrees instead of radians).
Remainder theorem: p(a) equals the remainder on division by x-a.
Direct-proportion rate "at this rate, how many..." (miles per gallon vs bottles per minutes); SAT 054 adds an hours-to-minutes conversion.
Both: constants making a one-variable linear equation degenerate; SAT 013 asks infinitely many solutions, SAT 029 no solution - same coefficient-matching idea.
Two item prices, total for a mix of items, find one item price (system vs. substitution with "costs $2 more").
Rewrite exponential expressions with a common base (9^(x/2)=3^x vs 4^(x/2)*8^(x/3)=2^(kx)).
Intersections of a line and a parabola; SAT asks greatest x-coordinate, ACT asks sum of x-coordinates.
Area of a right triangle/rectangle built from a Pythagorean triple (5-12-13 vs 7-24-25).
Circle in expanded form x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey=k, complete the square (SAT finds k from radius, ACT finds center/radius).
Both solve c - 2x vs constant with sign flip (3-2x>11 vs 7-2x<1); SAT 038 adds function notation and asks for the interval.
Exponential model with a multi-year period; SAT 026 interprets (1.05)^(t/2), SAT 102 converts 1.2^t to growth per 2 years.
Rational equation solved by cross-multiplying to a linear equation (4/(x-2)=2/(x-5) vs (a-1)/(a+4)=2).
Proportion with the variable on both sides, cross-multiply to linear.
Line given by slope and a point; SAT 028 finds y when x=0, SAT 058 finds x when y=12 - same point-slope routine.
ax+3 = cx+d with no solution, find condition on the coefficient (SAT is "which must be true" with two constants).
Factored form a(x-p)(x-q) with one extra condition used to find a (max value vs a point).
Population density recomputed after a change in population (SAT adds people; ACT merges towns).
Total from two subgroup conditional rates (60% of 140 + 30 vs weighted 25%/40%).
Right-triangle trig ratio requiring the missing side by Pythagoras (cos from hyp+leg vs sin from two legs).
Linear function from a table; SAT evaluates f(-4), ACT asks for the rule.
Use one known function value to find the constant, then evaluate at a different input.
Cofunction identity sin(theta)=cos(90-theta); SAT solves for k in angle expressions.
Demo fixture: choose an exponential model expression (triples every 4 hours, t in days) - SAT 061 lacks the unit twist.
Work backward from a discounted sale price to the original (SAT adds a markup layer).
Coefficient making two lines parallel / system with no solution via equal slopes.
Isolate a power of 2 and match exponents (3*2^(x+1)=96 vs 50*2^(t/3)=400).
Both are mean-via-total problems; SAT 084 replaces a value rather than adding one - same total-adjust reasoning, different ask.
Range of the constant for which a quadratic has two distinct real solutions (ACT adds both roots > 1).
Fixed amount plus/minus a per-period rate against a bound; find the whole-number count of periods.
Change one value in a list with known mean (replace vs drop) and find the new mean via totals.
Missing value from a known mean (SAT then takes the median).
Distance from a rate and a time with mismatched time units (pace in min/mile vs km/h for 25 min).
Rectangle from one dimension plus area/perimeter, find the other measure (inverse ask).
Translate "k more than m times a number" into a linear equation and solve.
Exponential factor over 2 units of input (1.2^2 = 1.44 vs 3^2 = 9).

summary: 64 flagged pairs: 3 copy, 26 template, 35 close. 25 distinct SAT items are in copy/template pairs. Internal SAT repeats: 001/091 (copy), 012/097, 004/051, 007/062 (template). Strongest cross-bank collisions: SAT 086 vs ACT 0466 and SAT 088 vs ACT 0351 (copy), plus SAT 042 (line tangent to parabola) which repeats both ACT 0665 and fixture act-math-12, SAT 007 which repeats both SAT 062 and ACT 0497 (all perfect-square b=12/k=6 family), and SAT 074 which repeats ACT 0530 and fixture act-math-05. Recommend rewriting or retiring one item in each copy pair and varying the asked quantity or setup for template pairs; close pairs are informational. ACT bank actually holds 795 items (not 774); all were compared. Template examples cited in the brief (inscribed/central angle algebra, 5:2 recipe) have no match inside the SAT bank: SAT 056 has no counterpart, and the 5:2 recipe item is ACT 0582 only.
